title: Leaflet template: three panels
subject: English
source: Written for english/y5 lesson 46 (Leaflet template: three panels (printable or tablet))
intro: Lesson 46: A leaflet guide to ancient Olympia (condensed lesson). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Plain
Persuasive
rows: Feel the ground shake as 40,000 spectators roar in the mighty stadium!

parts.text: Rhetorical question: Have you ever heard 40,000 people cheer at once?
Imperative: Take your place on the earth banks at dawn.
Fact: Watch the stadion, a sprint of about 192 m.
Persuasive close: Do not miss the most famous race in Greece!

keywords.def: a short printed sheet that informs or persuades
a bossy verb that gives a command: Visit, Watch, Explore
a question that makes the reader think, not one to answer
trying to make someone think or do something

questions.q: Make persuasive: The olive wreath is given to winners.
questions.a: For example: Watch the champion receive the famous olive wreath!

questions.q: Write a heading for the hippodrome section
questions.a: For example: Thunder of the Chariots

questions.q: Write a rhetorical question about the journey
questions.a: For example: Why not join the great procession from Elis?

questions.q: Core: write a two-section leaflet guide (Race Day and one more), with a title, headings, a rhetorical question and imperative verbs
Extend: add a fact box with three numbers
questions.a: For example: 192 m stadion; 40,000 spectators; every 4 years

questions.q: Stretch: use a relative clause in one section
questions.a: For example: Visit the stadium, where champions are crowned.

options: Explore the gymnasium where champions train!
questions.a: B) Explore the gymnasium where champions train!. B uses an imperative and an exciting detail. A and C only state facts.

questions.q: Leaflets often use imperative verbs to...
questions.a: A) tell the reader what to do
options: tell the reader what to do
